title: More Ultrawealthy in Trump's Administration Than in Previous Three Presidencies Combined
description_short: More Ultrawealthy in Trump's Administration Than in Previous Three Presidencies Combined
description_medium: A Public Citizen report cited by PBS found 57 Trump administration officials worth at least $100 million, more than four times the combined number in the previous three administrations. The group counted 17 ambassadors and 40 senior executive-branch officials; eight of 23 Cabinet members met its threshold. The report raised concerns about concentrated wealth and policy influence, but wealth alone does not establish a conflict or corrupt decision. The data uses a $100 million cutoff.
description_long:
A Public Citizen report cited by PBS found 57 people in Donald Trump’s administration with estimated wealth of at least $100 million. That count included 17 ambassadors and 40 senior officials across the executive branch, and eight of 23 Cabinet members met the threshold. PBS reported that the total was more than four times the combined count under the previous three presidents. The report highlighted Treasury Secretary Howard Lutnick and Education Secretary Linda McMahon among its billionaire Cabinet members.

The comparison drew attention to the scale of personal wealth among officials and renewed questions about how wealth and government service interact. It does not, by itself, show that an official made a decision to benefit a private interest or establish a specific conflict of interest. The number depends on Public Citizen’s threshold and calculations. The supported point is the report’s comparison of the Trump administration’s ultrawealthy appointees with earlier administrations, alongside broader concerns about influence and representation.

The court did not decide in this order whether the construction was lawful or who would ultimately prevail.
